transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-01 15:00 PST - Duration: ~47 minutes - Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Rajiv (Praxis Head of Platform), Sofia (Praxis Security Eng), Ethan (Praxis SRE), Marina (Product), Tom (Legal)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do quick intros--I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Liam and Priya from our engineering side. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Rajiv: good, thanks. lot to cover on security and key ops, hoping to understand how you handle CMKs and audit logs.
[00:20] Maya: perfect, that's why we asked for a focused intake. quick agenda: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML, RBAC, logs & retention, and KMS. then we'll align on hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:28] Sofia: yes, and timeline wise we need something in pilot by mid Q1. also legal will want retention policy details.
[00:36] Tom: yeah we'll need to review the controls mapping for SOC2; default cookie cutter answers don't cut it.
[00:45] Liam: great, I'll walk through technical support for keys and logs; Priya will follow with KMS patterns and rotation. FYI some terms might sound like "K-V cash" in auto transcribe, sorry in advance.

[01:02] Sofia: quick qualification: our prod data is regulated transit telemetry plus PII minimal. We need encryption at rest, field tokenization for PII, and strict key rotation. we prefer customer-managed keys in our cloud account.
[01:20] Priya: understood. Redwood supports CMK patterns: hosted with bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via cross-account KMS grants, Dedicated where the GPU fleet is in our VPC peered setup, and Private where the control plane is customer-managed. For HSM-backed keys, we integrate with cloud KMSes that support HSM (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault HSM, GCP Cloud KMS HSM).
[01:45] Ethan: do you require any key material to leave our cloud? we cannot export raw keys.
[01:52] Liam: no, keys never leave customer control in BYOK flows; Redwood uses envelope encryption model. small caveat when using Redwood hosted without BYOK, we manage keys and rotate them.

[02:10] Marina: pilot idea: dev team uses Hosted for speed, prod on Dedicated with BYOK. Is that a common setup?
[02:18] Maya: yes very common. dev on Hosted for agility, production on Dedicated or Private for isolation. costs/latency tradeoffs there too.

[02:35] Rajiv: SOC2 - we are requested to map controls for encryption, key mgmt, incident response, and audit logging. do you have SOC2 Type II and do you provide evidence packages?
[02:45] Maya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we provide a security snapshot for customers; for enterprise we can share auditor letters under NDA. We also provide per-tenant audit logs and retention options.
[02:58] Tom: what is included in the audit logs? we need user-level, token-level, model-invocation, and admin actions with timestamps.
[03:08] Priya: current audit surface includes API request logs (token id, route, model, latency, error), auth events (login, token create/delete), and admin actions in the console (role changes, key grants). We can push logs to your SIEM via S3 export + Kinesis or direct Splunk HEC in near-real-time.
[03:30] Sofia: retention defaults? we have policy for 7 years archival for certain records.
[03:36] Liam: Redwood default retention is 90 days in the console; for enterprise customers we support configurable retention and long-term archival to your S3 with lifecycle policies, or we can support a legal-hold export. 7 years is long but possible if you accept storage charges.

[03:55] Rajiv: RBAC - our org needs fine grained route-level control: certain tokens can call embeddings only, others can call generation, and dev/test tokens must not access production models.
[04:06] Priya: we have token scopes and role policies. tokens can be scoped to API routes and to model families. Admins can define roles in the Console or via our SCIM integration for mapping groups from your IdP. There's also per-token quotas and usage limits.
[04:23] Ethan: SCIM provisioning? We use Okta and jump cloud for provisioning.
[04:28] Liam: SCIM is supported; SAML 2.0 SSO for Login and SCIM for user/group provisioning. You can bind Okta groups to Redwood roles.

[04:45] Marina: does SAML support IdP-initiated flows and enforce MFA?
[04:50] Maya: yes, we support both SP and IdP initiated SAML and enforce whatever MFA policies your IdP sends. The Console respects SAML assertions for email and groups.

[05:02] Tom: legal question — how do you handle data residency? some routes can't leave EU.
[05:08] Liam: we support region pinning and can route requests to EU-hosted clusters. For Dedicated we can provision capacity in the region you require. Private on-prem is also an option for strict residency.

[05:25] Sofia: what about KV cache/key rotation implications — if we rotate keys frequently will cached state break for long-running sessions?
[05:33] Priya: great question. we use envelope encryption so rotating the data encryption keys doesn't require invalidating the tokenized KV cache. however if you rotate the master key and revoke access, the runtime needs rekeying for persisted KV; ephemeral in-memory caches not affected. There are operational playbooks to do rolling rekeys to avoid session churn.

[05:58] Rajiv: can you call out HSM-backed rotation frequency and constraints? our security team wants 90-day rotation with auditable key lifecycle.
[06:06] Liam: HSM-backed KMS supports scheduled rotation; for AWS KMS you can set automatic key rotation (yearly) or call RotateKey API programmatically. For 90-day rotation we'll recommend a rotation orchestration that updates grants and performs a controlled rewrap of data keys; we can provide scripts and an operator runbook.

[06:28] Sophia: (laughs) I keep getting auto transcript mislabels — but back to logs — can you tag logs with user email and token id? we need correlation for incident response.
[06:36] Priya: yes, logs include token id, request id, user metadata (when available), source IP, model id, and latency. We scrub payloads depending on PII settings, and provide a PII tokenization layer so raw PII never lands in logs if you enable it.

[06:58] Ethan: how are secrets stored in Dedicated deployments?
[07:03] Liam: secrets for Dedicated are stored using the customer's KMS when BYOK is configured; otherwise secrets are stored in our vault encrypted at rest. For Private deployments, everything is in your control.

[07:15] Marina: compliance evidence — can we map your controls to ours? are you open to filling a custom questionnaire?
[07:22] Maya: yes we regularly complete customer questionnaires (VSA/SSAE stuff). We'll use Redwoods security snapshot as a baseline and fill in your custom items. May need NDA for some attachments.

[07:35] Rajiv: competitors — we saw AlphaServe and CloudEdge proposals. main tie-breakers are cost per token and auditability.
[07:44] Maya: understood. Redwood focuses on predictable unit economics and strong observability. For auditability we provide tracebacks from token-level charges back to requests and store admin audit actions for the retention you specify.

[07:55] Tom: any special contractual SLAs around key management? if you host keys what guarantees exist for rotation and deletion?
[08:02] Liam: if Redwood manages keys we have documented key lifecycle procedures and we can commit to deletion/rotation windows but for cryptographic guarantees we recommend BYOK with your KMS. Host-managed keys are fine for lower-scope usecases but for legal/regulated workloads BYOK is standard.

[08:23] Sofia: question about log exports: do you support immutable append-only logs to our S3 with object lock? That's our E-Discovery requirement.
[08:31] Priya: yes we can export to S3 where you control the bucket ACLs and object lock. We can also forward to Kafka/Confluent or direct Splunk ingestion if you need streaming.

[08:45] Marina: do you have RBAC audit reports? senior leadership asks for review of access changes monthly.
[08:51] Maya: we can generate monthly RBAC change reports and provide them as CSV exports. Also Console shows a change history with actor and timestamp.

[09:02] Rajiv: can we see a demo of the audit UI and the key rotation playbook next call?
[09:07] Maya: yes we can demo. we'll include a short walkthrough of the Console audit view and a runthrough of a simulated key rotation.

[09:18] Sofia: also need to confirm that encryption-at-rest is FIPS 140-2 validated HSM path where required.
[09:24] Liam: we can integrate with FIPS-compliant HSM offerings from cloud providers. We'll call that out in the doc.

[09:33] Ethan: instrumentation: for perf-sensitive routes, will enabling detailed audit logs add a lot of latency?
[09:38] Priya: there is a small overhead for synchronous log calls; most customers use async batched exports to avoid latency hits. For strict low-latency SLOs we recommend sampling or async export. We can provide benchmarks.

[09:54] Maya: quick recap before diving into a few specifics — you want BYOK for prod, 90-day rotation playbook, audit log export to S3/Splunk with object lock, SCIM/Okta integration, RBAC route scoping, SOC2 evidence and questionnaire response, and a pilot timeline mid-Q1. Anything missing?
[10:12] Rajiv: plus token scoping for dev vs prod, and a formal cost estimate for Dedicated with reserved capacity.

[10:20] Priya: one more detail on token scoping: tokens are issued with scopes that limit routes and models and we can bind them to environment tags. We'll add a sample token policy in the follow-up.

[10:32] Marina: legal will want a data processing addendum and data retention table.
[10:37] Tom: yes, please include that.

[10:44] Liam: for the pilot we'll propose a small Dedicated pool in your preferred region and run a workload benchmark. we'll collect metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, failure rate, and cost per token.

[10:58] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up with a packet: security snapshot, KMS runbook, RBAC token policy sample, pilot scope, and pricing. Priya will share the KMS diagram and scripts.

[11:10] Rajiv: timeline for artifacts?
[11:12] Maya: we'll share initial artifacts by 2026-12-03 and ask to schedule the pilot kickoff the week of 2026-12-13.

[11:22] Sofia: one final question — do you support double-wrapping keys (customer key wraps service key wraps data key) for extra protection?
[11:30] Priya: yes envelope encryption supports double wrap where your CMK wraps the intermediate key we use. That pattern is standard and we'll document the grant management details.

[11:44] Ethan: ok sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:47] Maya: thanks all, we'll send notes.

End of meeting.
